examples.label: Same shell used to launch a reverse shell

notes: Only works on versions where the core PHP Filter module exists/can be enabled (Drupal 7). On Drupal 8+ use the backdoored-module or Drupalgeddon2 path instead.

recommended.note: Confirms the version supports the PHP filter module.
Newer Drupal: hide the shell inside a module instead.
Upgrade to an interactive reverse shell.

name: Drupal - PHP Filter Module Webshell
description: On Drupal versions with the PHP Filter module, create a node with PHP body input containing a system() call to gain RCE. On newer versions, install the PHP module first.

defense.why_it_works: Drupal's PHP Filter module (when enabled) allows admin users to create content nodes containing raw PHP code executed server-side. Adding a webshell as node content and visiting its URL executes arbitrary PHP.
defense.prerequisites: Valid Drupal admin credentials. PHP Filter module enabled. (Drupal 8+ requires manual installation of the php module.)
defense.impact: RCE as www-data via a content node. Persistent access through the CMS without touching the filesystem directly.
defense.detection: Node creation with text_format=php_code via admin. Unexpected PHP output in node response. Drupal watchdog log for content creation.
defense.artifacts: Drupal watchdog log (node created by admin) | Web server access log (GET to node with query param) | Database: nodes table containing PHP code
defense.splunk_spl:
index=sysmon EventCode=1 (ParentImage="*w3wp.exe" OR ParentImage="*httpd*" OR ParentImage="*apache*" OR ParentImage="*php*" OR ParentImage="*tomcat*" OR ParentImage="*java.exe") (Image="*cmd.exe" OR Image="*powershell.exe" OR Image="*sh")
| table _time, Computer, ParentImage, Image, CommandLine

index=sysmon EventCode=11 (TargetFilename="*.php" OR TargetFilename="*.aspx" OR TargetFilename="*.jsp") (TargetFilename="*upload*" OR TargetFilename="*webroot*")
| table _time, Computer, Image, TargetFilename
defense.elastic_kql: event.code:"1" AND process.parent.name:(w3wp.exe OR httpd OR apache2 OR php-fpm OR java.exe) AND process.name:(cmd.exe OR powershell.exe OR sh OR bash)
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("w3wp.exe","httpd","apache2","php-fpm","php-cgi","java.exe","tomcat")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","sh","bash")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, ProcessCommandLine
| union (DeviceFileEvents | where FileName endswith_any (".php",".aspx",".jsp") and FolderPath has_any ("upload","wwwroot","webroot","htdocs") | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, ProcessCommandLine=FolderPath)
| sort by Timestamp desc
// Drupal PHP-filter webshell - apache/php spawning a shell
defense.sigma_rules: web_shell_execution, file_event_web_shell_written (Drupal PHP-filter webshell - apache/php spawning a shell)
defense.prevention: Never enable the PHP Filter module in production. If required, restrict to a dedicated role not given to regular admins. Disable module entirely if possible.
defense.misconfiguration: PHP Filter module enabled in Drupal, allowing admin users to save and execute arbitrary PHP through the content interface.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Drupal -- PHP Filter module enabled (allows PHP in node content)
# /admin/modules -- PHP Filter module: [x] Enabled
# Any user with 'Use the PHP evaluator' permission can execute arbitrary code

# settings.php -- no restriction on who can create PHP nodes
$conf['filter_allowed_protocols'] = array('http', 'https', 'ftp', 'ftps', 'mailto', 'news', 'tel');
# php module enabled in modules/ directory and active
defense.secure_config:
# Drupal -- disable PHP Filter module entirely
# /admin/modules: PHP Filter module: [ ] Disabled

# If PHP execution is needed, restrict permission strictly:
# /admin/people/permissions:
#   Use the PHP evaluator: [ ] authenticated user
#                          [ ] editor
#                          [x] administrator only (and only if required)

# Better: use Twig templates instead of PHP filter
# Remove php.module from sites/all/modules/ entirely
# Verify in settings.php:
$settings['trusted_host_patterns'] = ['^www\.example\.com$'];
defense.evasion: Rename/obfuscate the uploaded webshell and delete it after use; prefer the app's built-in functionality (PHP filter / module) over dropping files; pace requests to blend with normal traffic.

explain:
Gains RCE on Drupal by posting PHP through the PHP Filter module:
  <?php system($_GET['<rand>']); ?>   a node body that executes the 'rand' query parameter as a shell command
Create a node with PHP input format enabled, then hit it with ?<rand>=id (or a reverse-shell one-liner); on newer Drupal you must install the PHP module first since it is no longer bundled.
